clauses.text: Belongs here if it asserts that this codebase reproduces what the pre-refactor code computed, at EITHER granularity — a unit-granularity value-equivalence test whose oracle is the legacy code's own values, or a run-granularity comparison between a preserved `pre_refactor_method` and its current sister — or if it rules a legacy unit scope-in, discard or scope-out, or registers, dispatches, records or enforces a sister pair or a divergence-ledger entry.
Does NOT belong here if its oracle is the manuscript (`publication-math-conformance`) or the observed record (`generator-validation`)
does NOT belong here if it is the reimplementation itself rather than the test or the pairing asserting it

does NOT belong here if it is an equivalence test for a scoped-IN unit, since those are scoped to the system owning the code under test, and a scope-out or discard carries no test, the disposition ledger's row checks verifying it instead
does NOT belong here if it is the toggle's per-run VALUE, which `run-configuration-and-provenance` holds
does NOT belong here if it concerns whether a reported test RESULT is interpretable, which is `test-result-legibility`'s, `test` in this row denoting the PYTEST sense of an executed member test
does NOT belong here if it executes the legacy tree, which `ADR-c` and `C-U28` forbid
Belongs here if it binds a manuscript equation to executable code, or classifies a paper/code divergence under the nine-class taxonomy.
Does NOT belong here if the discrepancy is between new and legacy code rather than between code and paper (`pre-refactor-correspondence`)

does NOT belong here if it binds a method this codebase implements to an EXTERNAL publication, or resolves which published methods a run exercised, or emits a citation set, which is `method-attribution`'s — this row's register binds an equation to a location in THIS PROJECT'S OWN manuscript and holds no external binding

does belong here, as an owned obligation rather than a routing case, to PUBLISH § B2's `Status` field under a CLOSED VOCABULARY, since `method-attribution` reads it as a declared interface and a consumer cannot make a producer's field well-formed from inside itself
does NOT belong here if it is an edit to the manuscript, which is hard-gated on the user and is never this system's act

Belongs here if it reconciles two or more source products into one record or establishes that they may be pooled — the coverage calendar, the resolution-equivalence resample, the priority-ordered merge, the distribution-equivalence gating.
Does NOT belong here if it fetches or pre-processes a source product, which is `hydro-fetch` upstream and outside this project
does NOT belong here if it decides what counts as an event within the assembled record (`combined-event-identification`)
Belongs here if it defines an event boundary, an event statistic, or an event-type label.
Does NOT belong here if it consumes an already-defined event set to fit, sample, synthesize or validate
does NOT belong here if it assigns a probability to a statistic this system defines (`event-frequency-assessment`)
Belongs here if it fits a univariate distribution to the event-statistic sample and selects on copula-input adequacy.

Does NOT belong here if it fits a distribution to assign exceedance probabilities and selects on upper-tail fidelity (`event-frequency-assessment` — same technique, different sample, purpose and acceptance test)
does NOT belong here if it concerns dependence across statistics
Belongs here if it concerns the copula's tree structure, its pair families, its fit diagnostics, or drawing from it.
Does NOT belong here if it concerns a single statistic's marginal, how many events occur, or what happens to a drawn statistic vector after it leaves the copula
Belongs here if it concerns event COUNTS, event timing, or the observed occurrence record those counts are resampled from.
Does NOT belong here if it concerns the MAGNITUDE of an event's statistics (`dependence-modelling`, `marginal-distribution-fitting`)
does NOT belong here if it is the data-availability calendar itself, which `observed-record-assembly` publishes and this system consumes
Belongs here if it converts statistics into a time series, or accepts or rejects a synthesized series on physical grounds.
Does NOT belong here if it decides what the statistics are or how many events there are
does NOT belong here if it serializes and publishes the finished series (`boundary-condition-output`)
Belongs here if it decides the shape, encoding or metadata of a published artifact, or mints an identifier that travels with it.
Does NOT belong here if it computes the values being published
does NOT belong here if it is a downstream consumer's adapter or equality validation, which consumers own
Belongs here if its oracle is the OBSERVED record and its question is whether the generated population matches it.
Does NOT belong here if its oracle is the legacy code (`pre-refactor-correspondence`) or the manuscript (`publication-math-conformance`)
does NOT belong here if the question is which candidate a user should CHOOSE (`interactive-decision-support`)

does NOT belong here if the question is whether a reported result of the member's own PYTEST suite is interpretable, which is `test-result-legibility`'s — `test` in THIS row denotes the STATISTICAL sense, a two-sample or Monte-Carlo test and its statistic
Belongs here if it presents evidence for a human CHOICE, or emits the identifiers recording that choice.
Does NOT belong here if it reports a verdict on a completed run (`generator-validation`)
does NOT belong here if it STORES the resulting selection, since the emitted artifact is held by `run-configuration-and-provenance`
Belongs here if it concerns the graph, a rule's place in it, an execution mode, or the reporting layer's mechanics.
Does NOT belong here if it is the computation a rule invokes
does NOT belong here if it is the CONTENT of a figure, since every system translates its own figures and this system delivers them
Belongs here if it DEFINES how a seed is supplied, how a run's provenance is recorded, or how a machine-specific path is resolved, or if it HOLDS a versioned per-run selection artifact.

Does NOT belong here if it is a call site that DRAWS a random number, or a system declaring its own identity into the provenance record — those live in the owning compute system's plan, which is why this system's Definition of Done is satisfiable only jointly with theirs. The SHAPE of the seed interface (`OD-3`) and of the self-declaration interface (`OD-5`) are this system's to settle; the implementations they govern are not

Belongs here if it decides whether the software can be INSTALLED or PINNED, or whether the toolkit can be cited BY others — the public API surface, a declared runtime dependency, a version pin, the licence, or a step of the release gate.
Does NOT belong here if it varies per RUN (`run-configuration-and-provenance`)

does NOT belong here if it decides whether the software can be UNDERSTOOD OR RUN by a reader who is not its author — narrative documentation, a runnable worked example, the rendered site, or the documentation test corpus — which is `documentation-and-examples`, and note that the earlier predicate "fixed per RELEASE" does NOT discriminate against that sibling because documentation is fixed per release too
does NOT belong here if it makes this toolkit CITE others, which is `method-attribution`'s and runs in the opposite direction
does NOT belong here if it is a system's internal documentation of its own computation
Belongs here if it fits a distribution in order to assign an exceedance probability, or computes a univariate event-statistic return period.
Does NOT belong here if it fits a marginal to feed the copula (`marginal-distribution-fitting`)
does NOT belong here if the probability is assigned to a FLOODING property rather than a WEATHER property, which stays with the flood project
does NOT belong here if it samples realizations at a stated return level (`monte-carlo-design-storms`)
Belongs here if it samples a realization at a STATED return level, or computes the return period defining that level for the sampling design.

Does NOT belong here if it fits the distribution being sampled (`event-frequency-assessment`), decides how many events occur in a period (`event-occurrence-modelling`), or converts a sampled statistic vector into forcing (`timeseries-synthesis`); and does NOT belong here as a second publication surface, since delivery is `boundary-condition-output`'s contract

Belongs here if it decides whether the software can be UNDERSTOOD OR RUN by a reader who is not its author — narrative documentation, a runnable worked example, the rendered site and its build, or the documentation test corpus.
Does NOT belong here if it decides whether the software can be INSTALLED OR PINNED, or whether the toolkit can be cited BY others (`packaging-and-release`)

does NOT belong here if it is the FACT a documented statement is generated from — a configuration field description or a docstring — which the owning system carries in its own code under this system's constraint arm, and that arm CLAIMS NO FILES

does NOT belong here if it is the CONTENT of the method-citation register, which `method-attribution` owns and this system may only render, on § 6.9's cut that documentation is about the SOFTWARE while a citation is about a CLAIM

Belongs here if it is an artifact class whose CONTENT is specific to one machine or one run, or the structure and READMEs by which such content is found, or the predicate assigning an artifact class its home, or the anonymization guard's count-only report mode in CI, which exists only so that the toolkit's CI can scan with the private token lists the estate holds. **Membership is decided by the OBJECT and NEVER by where a file sits**: residence in `[withheld]` is not a reason to route work here and residence in the toolkit repository is not a reason to route it away. The ecosystem clause defining this row is ported at `s6.5-private-estate`.
Does NOT belong here if it is the MECHANISM resolving a machine-varying path or recording provenance, which is `run-configuration-and-provenance`'s even though its concrete values are estate-side

does NOT belong here if it is an execution-mode binding, which is `workflow-orchestration`'s on the same ground; and this system's constraint arm CLAIMS NO FILES — it obliges every other system to declare which side of the boundary its artifacts fall on and claims none of theirs

Belongs here if it concerns what a reported result of THIS MEMBER'S OWN TEST SUITE means — which invocation a green is claimed against, the environment that invocation selected, the exclusion set derived from it against a named reference population, the subject resolution and the condition under which it would disagree, or the verdict the record carries. **`test` in this row denotes the PYTEST sense: an executed member test and its reported result.**

Does NOT belong here if it concerns a STATISTICAL test's output — a two-sample test, a Monte-Carlo tau test, a goodness-of-fit statistic or its p-value — which is `generator-validation`'s, where `test` denotes the statistical sense

does NOT belong here if it concerns WHAT a test asserts or which oracle it asserts against (`pre-refactor-correspondence`, `publication-math-conformance`, `generator-validation`); and this system's constraint arm CLAIMS NO FILES — its non-interference and provenance-bearing-shared-artifact invariants bind every other system's write roots and shared caches and claim none of their files

Belongs here if it records a published EXTERNAL source this codebase implements, binds such a source to the code implementing it, resolves which such sources a run exercised, or emits that set into a report.

Does NOT belong here if it binds an equation of THIS PROJECT'S OWN MANUSCRIPT to code, or classifies a divergence between this project's paper and its code, which is `publication-math-conformance`'s and whose predicate carries the converse limb naming this row.

Does NOT belong here if it is per-RUN state — inputs, seeds, or a compute system's implementation identity — which `run-configuration-and-provenance` holds, a published-method attribution being a property of the CODE and frozen with it

does NOT belong here if it is the delivery mechanics of the surface the citation section is rendered on (`workflow-orchestration`), or whether the toolkit can be cited BY others (`packaging-and-release`); and its constraint arm — every other system tags its methodological functions — CLAIMS NO FILES
